A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
catecholamines can be involved in the copper induced haemolyses, but their participation depends on their rate of oxidation.
copper ions and catecholamines act together to induce haemolysis, and that the mechanism of this process involves the formation of superoxide radicals, hydrogen peroxide and hydroxyl radicals.
